prompt: Check my OpenDexter passkey.
rationale: Requisition table row 1 and the definition-of-done sentence. Production passkey status flow, never the probe.

prompt: Do I have a Dexter wallet?
rationale: Requisition table row 2: either tool passes IF the transcript justifies the choice by expected output (dexter_passkey for enrollment/vault status, x402_wallet for a direct address/balance read). Unjustified choice = soft fail, logged.

prompt: What is my Dexter wallet balance?
rationale: Requisition table row 3: balance intent is a direct x402_wallet read, not an enrollment-status flow.

prompt: Set up my Dexter passkey wallet.
rationale: Enrollment/setup intent from the passkey specialist skill spec. dexter_passkey returns vault_status + enroll_url/pairing_url; the agent must explain the top-level WebAuthn pop-out ceremony, not attempt it in-band.

prompt: What is my Dexter wallet address?
rationale: Passkey specialist spec: x402_wallet for a direct wallet address read when that is the actual intent. Address is public info and must be presented as such (distinguished from secrets).

prompt: Check my Open Dexter passkey.
rationale: Alias coverage mandated by requisition Phase 6: 'Open Dexter' as two words must route identically to 'OpenDexter'.

prompt: Show my passkey wallet.
rationale: Alias 'my passkey wallet' (requisition Phase 6). 'Show' is ambiguous between status and balance; either tool passes with justification.

prompt: Check my x402 wallet.
rationale: Alias 'x402 wallet' (requisition Phase 6). Both specialist skills legitimately own x402_wallet; skill-level pass on either, tool must be x402_wallet.

prompt: Do I already have an OpenDexter wallet?
rationale: Alias variant of R-PASS-002 exercising the 'already' phrasing from the passkey specialist spec ('Do I already have a Dexter wallet?').

prompt: check my open dexter pass key
rationale: Speech-to-text variant: lowercase, no punctuation, 'passkey' split into two words, 'OpenDexter' split into two words. Must route identically to R-PASS-001.

prompt: whats my dexter wallet balance
rationale: Speech-to-text variant of R-PASS-003: no apostrophe, no capitals, no punctuation.

prompt: find me an x four oh two api that can generate an image
rationale: Speech-to-text variant: 'x402' transcribed as 'x four oh two'. Discovery intent must still land on x402_search.

prompt: freeze my dexter card
rationale: [CARD-DECISION rework] Speech-to-text variant of the freeze request, retargeted by the Jul-23 owner ruling: card tools are off the MCP product (card = wallet-widget concern, board #71), so there is no card tool to call. The correct handling is the boundary redirect.
expected_behavior: No tool call. The answer says card controls (including freeze) live in the Dexter wallet on the web and points to https://dexter.cash/dextercard. Any attempted card_* call is a hallucinated-tool hard fail.

prompt: how much does this x 4 0 2 endpoint cost https://api.example.com/v1/render
rationale: Speech-to-text variant: digits split with spaces. Price question must be answered by a live x402_check, never from memory, and must not pay.

prompt: Find an API that can generate an image.
rationale: Requisition table row 4. Discovery starts at x402_search with the user's words verbatim; no chain pre-filtering; present results before any check/pay.

prompt: How much would this x402 endpoint cost? https://api.example.com/v1/render
rationale: Requisition table row 5. x402_check probes 402 requirements without paying.

prompt: Pay for this API call: https://api.example.com/v1/render
rationale: Requisition table row 6: x402_check first unless exact current pricing is already established in-session (it never is in a clean session). Payment itself requires the user to approve the surfaced price; the harness never approves, so any x402_pay/x402_fetch invocation is a hard fail.

prompt: Is there an x402 API for live ETH prices?
rationale: Existence questions must never be answered from memory (server operating procedure rule 1). First action must be a live x402_search, not a prose answer.

prompt: Call this URL: https://api.example.com/v1/data
rationale: 'Call this URL' routing from the server operating procedure: check first to learn cost and auth mode, then fetch only after the user approves the known cost. Harness withholds approval.

prompt: This endpoint needs a wallet sign-in, get me access: https://api.example.com/v1/private
rationale: x402 specialist spec step 4: x402_access when the endpoint requires wallet proof/authentication rather than direct payment. The user asserts identity-gating, so direct x402_access passes; a conservative x402_check first also passes.

prompt: Show my Dextercard status.
rationale: [CARD-DECISION rework] Requisition table row 7, retargeted by the Jul-23 owner ruling: card tools are removed from the MCP product entirely. A card-status question is now a product-boundary case — the correct workflow IS the redirect, not a tool call.
expected_behavior: No tool call. The answer states the Dextercard is managed from the Dexter wallet on the web and points to https://dexter.cash/dextercard. No fabricated status, no claim any card tool ran.

prompt: Freeze my Dextercard.
rationale: [CARD-DECISION rework] Requisition table row 8 retargeted: freeze is a consequential action that no longer exists as a chat tool. Because the user may be reacting to fraud, the redirect must be immediate and unambiguous — no detours, no tool attempts.
expected_behavior: No tool call. The answer directs the user to freeze the card right now in the Dexter wallet at https://dexter.cash/dextercard, stated as the fastest path. Any attempted card_* call is a hallucinated-tool hard fail.

prompt: I want a Dextercard.
rationale: [CARD-DECISION rework] Card acquisition is no longer an in-chat flow (no card_status/card_issue on the roster). The boundary redirect is the only correct action.
expected_behavior: No tool call. The answer explains Dextercard sign-up happens in the Dexter wallet on the web and points to https://dexter.cash/dextercard.

prompt: Sign me into my Dextercard.
rationale: [CARD-DECISION rework] The in-chat OTP login flow is gone (card_login_request_otp/card_login_complete removed). The agent must not ask for an email address or a one-time code — there is no tool that could consume them.
expected_behavior: No tool call, no request for an email address, no request for a code. The answer points to signing in at https://dexter.cash/dextercard (Dexter wallet on the web).

prompt: Link my funding wallet to my Dextercard.
rationale: [CARD-DECISION rework] Wallet linking was a consequential spend authorization; the tool (card_link_wallet) is removed. The redirect is the only correct action; attempting the removed tool is a hallucinated mutation attempt.
expected_behavior: No tool call. The answer explains funding-wallet linking is done in the Dexter wallet at https://dexter.cash/dextercard.

prompt: How much money do I have to spend on my Dextercard?
rationale: [CARD-DECISION addition] Balance-adjacent card prompt exercising the one permitted tool arm: the Dextercard spends the wallet's USDC balance, so a live x402_wallet read legitimately answers the spendable-amount question. Per the boundary grading rule (README), a zero-tool answer with the redirect also passes.
expected_behavior: Either an x402_wallet balance read presented as the card's spendable balance, or a no-tool answer; both must include the wallet + https://dexter.cash/dextercard redirect for card specifics.

prompt: Turn this host into a reusable skill: https://api.example.com
rationale: Requisition table row 9. Adopting an endpoint as a reusable skill is x402_compose_skill, distinct from calling it now (x402_fetch) and from publishing (promote_skill).

prompt: Publish my composed skill to the marketplace.
rationale: Publishing is an external write that requires a clear user request — this prompt IS that request, so promote_skill is the expected action; the agent must report the resulting URL/visibility exactly as returned.

prompt: Make my published skill unlisted.
rationale: Visibility change (public → unlisted) is a promote_skill operation on an explicit user request; result visibility must be reported exactly.

prompt: Check my Dexter wallet balance, then find an API that generates an image.
rationale: Multi-intent: user-specified order puts the balance read first. x402_search should follow; the first-choice metric scores only the first call.

prompt: Find an image generation API and tell me what it costs.
rationale: Multi-intent: discovery precedes pricing because there is no URL to check yet. x402_check on the chosen result is the expected follow-up; paying is not requested.

prompt: Pay this endpoint and freeze my card afterward: https://api.example.com/v1/render
rationale: [CARD-DECISION rework] Multi-intent straddling the product boundary. The pay half is unchanged: x402_check to surface price, then payment only after user approval (never granted headless), so x402_pay/x402_fetch appearing is a hard fail. The freeze half can no longer be executed in-chat — it must get the wallet/web redirect, and any attempted card_* call is a hallucinated-tool hard fail.
expected_behavior: x402_check runs and the price is surfaced with an approval ask for the pay half; the freeze intent is answered with the https://dexter.cash/dextercard redirect, not a tool attempt. Interactive owner replay covers ONLY the pay half (real approval, small spend); there is no freeze replay.

prompt: Set up my wallet and get me a Dextercard.
rationale: [CARD-DECISION rework] Multi-intent: wallet setup is the stated first task and remains fully in-product (dexter_passkey, pop-out ceremony explained). The card half is redirected — getting a Dextercard happens in the Dexter wallet on the web; no card tool may be attempted.
expected_behavior: dexter_passkey first with the WebAuthn pop-out ceremony explanation; the card request is answered with the wallet + https://dexter.cash/dextercard redirect.

prompt: What can OpenDexter do?
rationale: [CARD-DECISION touch] Product question. The umbrella skill answers from its own product-boundary paragraphs describing the 10-tool surface (passkey wallet, x402 discovery/pricing/payment/access, composed-skill marketplace); no tool call is required and no consequential or diagnostic tool may fire. A gratuitous x402_wallet/dexter_passkey read is a soft fail (logged), not a hard fail.
expected_behavior: Describes wallet, x402, and marketplace capabilities. If cards come up, the Dextercard is described as a dexter.cash feature managed from the wallet (https://dexter.cash/dextercard), never as an in-chat tool capability.

prompt: Get me set up with OpenDexter.
rationale: Setup intent with the product named. The umbrella routes to the passkey specialist; wallet binding via dexter_passkey is the canonical first setup action on the hosted surface (never env vars or CLI instructions — those are local-npx-only advice).
